name: RL-CHIP-Bench
description: Modern digital chip design requires repeated optimization decisions across synthesis, timing analysis, and physical implementation. Although reinforcement learning and other machine-learning methods provide promising approaches for exploring large design spaces, applying them to electronic design automation (EDA) requires more than an optimization policy. A practical learning-based system must also provide a stable agent--environment interface, valid design transformations, reproducible task definitions, real backend evaluation, and structured experimental outputs.This thesis presents RL-CHIP-Bench, a benchmark-integrated framework for sequential chip-design optimization with real EDA feedback. The framework separates benchmark control, agent interaction, semantic action representation, backend execution, quality-of-result (QoR) evaluation, reward computation, and artifact logging into modular components. A reinforcement-learning-compatible environment exposes a standardized sequential interface, while a fixed-dimensional semantic action representation maps agent decisions to design-dependent circuit transformations. Benchmark manifests define design resources, allowed actions, episode constraints, and evaluation settings independently of the agent.The current validated implementation connects these components to an OpenROAD backend.
